title: Cap rate in 90 seconds, with a worked example
purpose: Educational explainer; supports the live product 'Rental Property Deal Analyzer' (B14-002). Internal review pilot, not authorized for publication. Educational only, not financial advice.

scenes.heading: What a cap rate measures
lines: A capitalization rate compares a property's yearly net operating income with its price.
It shows the return the property itself produces, before any mortgage.

scenes.heading: Step 1: net operating income
lines: Take a home renting for two thousand dollars a month: twenty-four thousand a year.
Allow five percent for empty months, which removes twelve hundred dollars.
Subtract operating costs such as taxes, insurance, repairs and management: seven thousand eight hundred.
That leaves a net operating income of fifteen thousand dollars.

scenes.heading: Step 2: divide by the price
lines: If the price is two hundred and fifty thousand dollars, divide fifteen thousand by that price.
The cap rate is six percent.

scenes.heading: What it leaves out

items: Mortgage payments are not in NOI
Big future repairs need their own reserve
Compare only with similar properties in the same area

lines: Mortgage payments are not part of net operating income, so the cap rate ignores financing.
Large future repairs need their own reserve.
Use it to compare similar properties in the same area. This is education, not financial advice.
